title: How do I improve Claude from making models from blender
author: Susmansusus
selftext: I'm using fable 5.2 medium since opus guided by fable doesn't make that nice. As you can see the reference picture doesn't make an accurate model, is there any prompting or skills to make Claude make better models?

comments.author: Ok_Feedback4200
comments.body: lol. check your references. It's modeling what you are giving it..

replies.author: Susmansusus
replies.body: Left is my reference picture, would it be better if I just feed one reference picture instead of different angle?

replies.author: Ok_Feedback4200
replies.body: It would be better if your different angle shots showed the same item in your references. The two little ones on the right don't make sense and that's what claude modeled...

replies.author: TopTippityTop
replies.body: Not really. It kind of got the gist, but executed it wrongly.

comments.author: Thin-Lie-1612
comments.body: The reference picture makes no sense btw. Fable did it better. I guess you mean the  darker outlines and shadow that is different.

comments.author: kamilr641
comments.body: the grinder in your image has the hopper and the wheel all over the place between views. try giving claude one reference sheet and ask it to compare each render against it and fix one part at a time. my guess is that it drifts when it tries to fix everything at once

comments.author: TopTippityTop
comments.body: In general, llms aren't quite good at this yet. Fable 5.2 is better, but not yet excellent. The best approach right now is to use a generative 3D model, and if needed then use Opus to bake it down to a low poly mesh.
